body:
## What is wanted

One map of the automated tasks in the delivery lifecycle, from ideation to a merged pull request and on into post-merge work. For each task it states:

- whether the skill behind it runs as its own run or as a step in an existing run;
- which component it belongs to: tracker, git host, runner, orchestrator or observability;
- its trigger, inputs and outputs, so tasks stay modular and can be composed.

## How the map is built

Through interviews with the owner, run with `/planning:wayfind`: one decision at a time, each answered by the owner. Repository data (transcripts, the plugin inventory, run records) is research input to those interviews. It does not settle a decision on its own, and a provisional answer drawn from it does not stand in for the owner's.

## Why

Skills and lanes have grown one at a time. Nothing shows the whole sequence, so gaps, overlaps and work that could share a run are hard to see, and each new lane adds load to a shared GitHub API budget.

## First item on the map

A simplify pass on every pull request, so that it no longer has to be done locally. Placement is open: a step inside the pull request, or a post-merge run with its own pull request. Choose whichever is most efficient. It must never slow the pull request.

## Research inputs

- Skill use recorded in session transcripts.
- The full plugin inventory, placed across the lifecycle.
- Work done per agent and per Actions run.

## Open question

Does this need a UI over the lifecycle, or are the map and the existing reports enough? The map should supply the evidence for that decision.

## Deferred items for the map

### A merge starts the next run

**What it is:** a merge on the git host starts the next run, so the work adapts its pace to how fast the developer wants to move that day.

**Why it is deferred:** it is a strong accelerator, so it stays open. Merges here are already unattended, so a merge-started run could start further agent work with no person in the loop. The map must decide its brakes before any task starts this way.

### Vendor-agnostic providers

**What it is:** the direction for how the factory is built:

- Vendor-agnostic and dependency-inverted, with providers you bring plus built-in implementations.
- Public repositories per concern: runner, orchestrator and observability.
- Tracker and git host are wired-up providers and are never rebuilt.
- One shared system, rather than separate ones for work and personal use.

**Why it is deferred:** this is direction without a design yet. The map is where it gets one.

### Runner choice per task

**What it is:** each task may run on the runner class that fits it, for example a cheap hosted CI runner for review and an isolated VM for implementation. Today one runner class serves every lane.

**Why it is deferred:** it changes the shape of the automation, and the map decides which tasks exist and where each runs before any task gets its own runner class.

### A factory spec handed to an agent

**What it is:** a written spec of the whole factory, complete enough that an agent can build it and run it.

**Why it is deferred:** the map is the input such a spec would describe, so the spec follows the map.

### A factory plugin

**What it is:** a plugin that ships skills to build, maintain, curate, update and extend a factory, for any downstream repository, this one included. This repository holds the beginnings of one.

**Why it is deferred:** which skills it ships follows from the tasks on the map.

### Two runner designs for building a spec

**What it is:** two ways to build a set of dependent tickets unattended:

- one runner per frontier, whose subagents build the unblocked tickets in parallel on one machine and one checkout, with no merge step;
- one runner per ticket, each isolated on its own machine, with a merger runner that combines their branches.

The first shares one environment and needs no merge; the second keeps each ticket's failure and changes apart at the cost of a merge step and a runner per ticket. Neither is preferred yet.

**Why it is deferred:** the choice depends on where the map places implementation and review, and on the runner question above.

### Vendor research for runners, storage and hosting

**What it is:** research of the runner, storage and hosting vendors a factory could use, what each does, and current alternatives to each.

**Why it is deferred:** public repositories stay on Actions and nothing is being bought now. The research belongs to the infrastructure design this map leads into, run as a `/planning:wayfind` effort.

## Decision items from the workshop 08 alignment pass (2026-11-24)

The owner sent these here to be decided with him, each as its own item. Run the first two first.

1. **Simplicity audit.** Run `/overengineering:audit` and compare our workflows with the course's four (43 workflows and 57,947 lines against 1,727), looking for duplication and over-engineering. Its findings become the next items. No line-count ceiling until then.
2. **One knob block per lane.** Every lane gets the same three settings (on/off, open-item cap, cadence), checked by one shared script before any model runs. Triggers are filtered so a run that would only skip never starts: `intake-reenter` ran 486 times on 2026-11-24 and skipped 468, and about 12,600 runs on 2026-11-22 were mostly skipped fan-out.
3. **Lane renames by responsibility,** starting with `pr-refine`, which only runs `fix-docs`. Each rename touches 58 to 240 files.
4. **Split lanes with more than one reason to change:** intake (verdict, admission, refinement, size split), work-unblock (unblock, status sync, re-fire), and pr-unblock (conflicts, feedback, dependency review, CI fixes).
5. **Terms with several meanings:** "triage" names four things and "refine" three; `status: confirmed` means verified in `/work-items:triage` and parked in the pipeline.
6. **Issue state** as an org field or as labels. The owner's model: a `needs-<thing>` label as the command, an in-progress state per activity, and a past-tense label as the event. Event-driven, with no polling; chains may fork and join.
7. **The dossier branch's** role across the lifecycle.
8. **A "needs a prototype" intake exit,** as the course does, before the spec.
9. **Rename `docs/conventions/pr-pipeline.yaml`** to match its real scope. It configures every lane, not only the PR pipeline.

Built outside the map, each as a session-owned issue: #18859 (intake on the skill-activity path), #18860 (one lane id list and stage vocabulary), #18861 (collaborative canvas mode), #18862 (the architecture scan), #18863 (lane output format), #18858 (a guardrails bug).

## Done when

The map is committed, each task on it has the fields above, the UI question has a recorded answer, and every deferred item has a recorded outcome.
